bibl.title: Distinct neural markers for intentional and unintentional task unrelated thought

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes.

span.label: task-unrelated thought (mind-wandering)
span.quote: The present study used EEG to seek support for these component-process accounts by examining the neural correlates of deliberate and spontaneous task unrelated thought.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Electroencephalography (EEG) was used to record ongoing brain activity during this period.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Deliberate off-task thought raises alpha activity, which inhibits irrelevant sensory input in a top-down manner and thereby protects the internally generated train of thought.
span.note: status: the paper's own words: may reflect
span.quote: We found that when participants were engaged in deliberate off-task thought, alpha activity was increased, a pattern that is often observed when individuals are deliberately engaged in internal tasks 71,110,118, and may reflect patterns of top down inhibition of irrelevant sensory input.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Spontaneous off-task thought arises because top-down maintenance of the task set fails, which shows up as jointly reduced P2 (higher-order perceptual processing) and N2 (conflict monitoring) responses.
span.quote: The combination of reduced P2 and N2 linked with spontaneous off-task thought suggests that this aspect of off-task experience may be associated with failure in the top down maintenance of the appropriate task set.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Intention determines whether executive control is being used to organise the internal train of thought or is intermittently failing: deliberate off-task states reflect motivated maintenance of a task set, spontaneous ones reflect lapses in maintaining it.
span.quote: In particular, based on our data we may expect that deliberate off-task thought is linked to the motivated maintenance of a task set, while more spontaneous off-task episodes are linked to intermittent failures to maintain task set in attention.

span.label: The four-trial pre-probe window is an a priori choice, since the true onset of an attentional shift is unknown.
span.note: what this limits: the attentional-state assignment: ALTHOUGH THE TEMPORAL DYNAMICS AND THE EXACT ONSET OF ATTENTIONAL SHIFTS REMAIN UNKNOWN AND DIFFICULT TO ASSESS, WE CHOSE A WINDOW OF FOUR SART TRIALS PRIOR TO A THOUGHT PROBE
span.quote: Although the temporal dynamics and the exact onset of attentional shifts remain unknown and difficult to assess31, we chose a window of four SART trials prior to a thought probe as reflecting the reported attentional state.

span.label: The self-caught probe condition structurally lacks on-task reports, so the two condition pairs are not symmetric.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison between the self-caught and probe-caught conditions: PARTICIPANTS WERE ONLY INSTRUCTED TO TRIGGER A SC PROBE WHEN THEY CAUGHT THEMSELVES OFF-TASK AND AS A RESULT THE SC CONDITION LACKED ON-TASK REPORTS
span.quote: Due to the nature of the task, participants were only instructed to trigger a SC probe when they caught themselves off-task and as a result the SC condition lacked on-task reports.

span.label: Trial-count exclusions cut the on-task versus off-task comparison to 15 participants.
span.note: what this limits: the PC_OT/MW comparison only: PARTICIPANTS THAT DID NOT HAVE AT LEAST 8 TRIALS WERE NOT CONSIDERED WHICH REDUCED THE NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS FOR THE PC_OT/MW PAIR TO 15
span.quote: For subsequent analyses participants that did not have at least 8 trials (amounting to a total of 32 epochs) for both conditions of a condition pair were not considered which reduced the number of participants for the PC_OT/MW pair to 15.

span.label: The most established marker in this literature does not distinguish the two states the paper is about: it is attenuated off-task whether the thought was intentional or not.
span.note: what this limits: a P3 attenuation as evidence about the KIND of off-task state: this study reports the P3 attenuated during off-task states regardless of whether they were intentional
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not.

span.label: The artefact-rejection threshold is a choice, and the authors state which way they wanted it to err.
span.note: what this limits: the artefact-cleaned data in this study: components were rejected at a 95% probability threshold chosen to favour preserving neural activity, so the cleaning errs toward keeping signal
span.quote: threshold for rejection was set at a conservative 95% probability to favor preservation of neural activity

span.label: Channels were excluded on a stated susceptibility argument rather than on measured artefact.
span.note: what this limits: the channel coverage of these averages: channels near the face were excluded on the grounds of higher susceptibility to artefacts
span.quote: channels in close proximity to the face were excluded on the grounds of a higher susceptibility to artifacts

span.label: The paper's central distinction is instrument-relative and the abstract says so in consecutive sentences: the P3 treats deliberate and spontaneous off-task thought as one state, alpha power and phase-locking treat them as two.
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not. In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes

span.label: probe-caught sampling prompts interrupting the task pseudo-randomly after 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42 or 48 trials
span.note: eliminates: participants anticipating the probe and preparing an answer - a fixed interval would turn a measure of spontaneous thought into a measure of expectation
span.quote: Probe-caught (PC) sampling prompts pseudo-randomly interrupted the task after 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42 or 48 trials (approx.

span.label: task unrelated thought
span.quote: Our study set out to explore the common and distinct neurocognitive processes that underlie patterns of intentional and unintentional off-task states, deliberate (dTUT) and spontaneous task-unrelated thought (sTUT) respectively.

span.label: dTUT
span.quote: deliberate (dTUT) and spontaneous task-unrelated thought (sTUT) respectively.

span.label: P3
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not.

span.label: alpha power
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not. In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes

span.label: sTUT
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not. In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes

span.label: task-unrelated thought - DELIBERATE (dTUT): the off-task state engaged in intentionally, one of two kinds the study separates
span.quote: Our study set out to explore the common and distinct neurocognitive processes that underlie patterns of intentional and unintentional off-task states, deliberate (dTUT) and spontaneous task-unrelated thought (sTUT) respectively.

span.label: task-unrelated thought - AS THE P3 SEES IT: not two kinds at all, since the component is attenuated off-task regardless of intention
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not.

span.label: theta ITPC - a phase-coherence quantity INTERPRETED as a measure of attentional stability, so the construct enters by interpretation rather than by measurement
span.quote: Theta ITPC, interpreted as a measure of attentional stability84, was found to be decreased in the parietal cortex

span.label: off-task thought - framed by the field it comes from as 'a family of states with overlapping experiential neural and cognitive features' rather than as a category with members
span.quote: Recent views from both psychology 24 and neuroscience25 have argued that off-task experiences can be understood as a family of states with overlapping experiential neural and cognitive features

span.label: P3 reduction - offered as an index of EITHER perceptual decoupling OR the level of attention to the task, in one clause, without adjudication
span.quote: reduction of the P3 amplitude, which can be considered an index of perceptual decoupling or the level of attention directed towards the task at hand

span.label: replicates → prior ERP studies of reduced stimulus processing during task-unrelated thinking (refs 26, 36, 38, 39)
span.quote: These results support prior studies that show reduced processing of stimuli in this time range for both online and offline measures of task unrelated thinking26,36,38,39.

span.label: builds-on → component process accounts of ongoing thought
span.quote: Consistent with component process accounts of ongoing thought these data suggest that periods of off-task thought with different experiential features depend on a different balance of neural processes.

span.label: builds-on → prior work linking spontaneous off-task thought to low external alertness and low executive control (ref 117)
span.quote: This interpretation seems to be consistent with prior studies that suggest that spontaneous off-task thought is primarily linked to lack of external alertness and lower executive control117.

span.label: dTUT —distinct-from→ sTUT
span.note: differs in: WHICH INSTRUMENT IS ASKED. Alpha power and cortical phase-locking separate them; the P3 does not, being attenuated off-task regardless of intention. The distinction the paper's title asserts holds on two measures and fails on the one the literature relies on most · strength of the relation: 0.9 — WHETHER THESE ARE TWO KINDS OF THOUGHT OR ONE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH MEASURE IS ASKED, and the paper's abstract puts both answers in consecutive sentences. The P3 - the literature's most established marker, and the record already carries a limitation saying so - is attenuated off-task 'REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THEY WERE INTENTIONAL OR NOT', so on that instrument the two states are ONE. Alpha power and cortical phase-locking separate them. A category claim that is true of one instrument and false of another, in one dataset.
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not. In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes

span.label: P3 —operationalised-as→ task unrelated thought
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — The P3 reduction is read as 'an index of perceptual decoupling or the level of attention directed towards the task at hand' - TWO different readings offered in one clause, joined by `or`, and the paper does not choose between them.
span.quote: reduction of the P3 amplitude, which can be considered an index of perceptual decoupling or the level of attention directed towards the task at hand

span.label: alpha power —operationalised-as→ dTUT
span.quote: Event-related potentials, such as the P3, were attenuated during off-task states, regardless of whether they were intentional or not. In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes

span.label: repeated-measures ANOVA
span.quote: Parieto-occipital ERP contrasts were evaluated with 2*2*3 repeatedmeasures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with factors condition (COND) x channel location (LOC) x ERP component/ time interval (TIME).

span.label: paired-samples t-test
span.quote: For simple contrasts, e.g., channel FCz with two conditions, and post-hoc testing, paired sample t-tests were conducted.

span.label: cluster-based permutation test
span.quote: To precisely determine channels and time-intervals exhibiting significant differences across conditions cluster-based permutation testing (allowing for a more accurate approximation of the Monte-Carlo statistic and correcting for multiple comparisons) was conducted as proposed by Maris & Oostenveld100 and implemented in Fieldtrip.

span.label: Monte-Carlo randomisation null distribution
span.quote: The significance of the difference between two compared condition, the Monte-Carlo p-value, is estimated by comparing the observed cluster-level statistic with a randomization null distribution, obtained here from 3000 random draws, under the assumption of no differences between conditions.

span.label: Greenhouse-Geisser sphericity correction
span.quote: We report Greenhouse-corrected p-values whenever sphericity was violated.

span.label: significance level
span.quote: The overall alpha level was set at 0.05.

span.label: independent component analysis
span.quote: ICA, a blind-source separation method, was applied with EEGLAB 13 to extract independent components, which were subsequently inspected and automatically label with MARA96

span.label: mean and standard deviation
span.quote: Twenty-six participants (12 females, age M: 25 SD: 4.3) with no history of neurological or psychiatric disease volunteered or received partial course credits to participate in the study.

span.label: Probe-caught off-task periods showed reduced P1 and P2 amplitude over the right parieto-occipital site PO4 and reduced amplitude over parieto-central sites in the P3 window (268-388 ms).
span.quote: To sum up, the PC_OT/MW condition pair revealed a right parieto-central attenuation as observed by a reduction in P1 and P2 amplitude over PO4 and reduced amplitude over parieto-central sites for the P3 time-interval (268 - 388 msec; see Figure 2).

span.label: Alpha power in the trials preceding a report was significantly higher before deliberate off-task thought (1.54 dB) than before spontaneous off-task thought (0.58 dB).
span.quote: Follow-up t-tests determined alpha activity (Figure 5, C and supplemental Figure 2, right panel) to be significantly higher during dTUT pre-trials (M:1.54 dB SD: 1.44) when compared to sTUT (M:.58 dB SD: 1.2) [t(17)=2.25 p=.038].

span.label: Inter-trial phase coherence was significantly greater before deliberate than before spontaneous off-task thought (.52 vs .45 across all averaged channels).
span.quote: Lastly, two-tailed t-tests were found to be significant for ITPC values for all averaged channels [t(17)=2.8 p=.012] with increased coherence for dTUT (M: .52; SD: .1) relative to sTUT (M: .45; SD: .1)

span.label: The P2 component was significantly smaller before spontaneous than before deliberate off-task thought at both PO3 and PO4.
span.quote: Post-hoc t-tests showed significantly decreased amplitude for the sTUT condition for the P2 component on both PO3 (dTUT M:5.01µV SD: 4.41; MW M: 3.64µV SD: 3.01)[t(17)=2.4 p=.028] and PO4 (dTUT M: 4.44µV SD: 3.73; MW M: 3.56µV SD: 2.62)[t(17)=2.61 p=.018].

span.label: Fronto-central delta/theta power at FCz was significantly lower relative to baseline before off-task reports (-2.69 dB) than before on-task reports (-1.89 dB).
span.quote: Delta/theta power (thereafter referred to as FMT) measured at FCz [t(14)=2.45 p=.028], showed a significant decrease for the TUT condition (M:-2.69 dB SD: 1.24) relative to OT (M:-1.89 dB SD: .95) (Figure 3, right panel).

span.label: The stimulus-evoked alpha-beta event-related desynchronization differed by attentional state, reaching -2.27 dB before off-task reports versus -1.13 dB before on-task reports.
span.quote: T-tests unveiled a significantly decreased alpha-beta ERD (Figure 3, B) for MW pre-trials (M:-2.27 dB SD: 1.55) in comparison with OT pre-trials (M:-1.13 dB SD: 1.26) [t(14)=2.27 p=.039].

span.label: Inter-trial phase coherence did not distinguish on-task from off-task states in any of the three electrode sets, so the phase-coherence effect was specific to the deliberate/spontaneous contrast.
span.quote: T-tests for the ITPC values for all three sets of electrodes tested (all averaged nonboundary channels, FCz and PO3/4) failed to return significant differences for the PC_OT/MW condition pair.

span.label: Tonic (non-evoked) alpha power showed no significant on-task versus off-task difference at any electrode selection.
span.quote: The difference in tonic alpha power did not reach statistical significance for any of the tested channel constellations.

span.label: Off-task thought attenuated evoked potentials whether or not it was intentional, while alpha power and phase-locking rose specifically for deliberate off-task thought and evoked sensory responses dropped specifically for spontaneous off-task thought.
span.quote: In contrast, increased alpha power and cortical phase-locking were linked to deliberate off-task thoughts, while reductions of evoked sensory response were prevalent in spontaneous off-task episodes.

span.label: inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC)
span.quote: The phase or inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC) is a measure of the similarity in phase angle of the oscillation across trials hence bound between 0, no phase clustering, and 1, complete phase clustering across trials.

span.label: deliberate (dTUT) and spontaneous (sTUT) task-unrelated thought
span.quote: Our study set out to explore the common and distinct neurocognitive processes that underlie patterns of intentional and unintentional off-task states, deliberate (dTUT) and spontaneous task-unrelated thought (sTUT) respectively.

span.label: probe-caught (PC) thought probe
span.quote: PC probes consists of interruptions of the experimental task at random intervals prompting participants to reveal the content of their thoughts just prior to the interruption91.

span.label: self-caught (SC) thought probe
span.quote: SC probes require participants to monitor their attention and to interrupt the task as soon as they become aware of their mind straying92.

span.label: component process account of ongoing thought
span.term: component process account of ongoing thought
span.quote: One approach to explaining the apparent heterogeneity of the off-task state assumes that different types of experience emerge from variation in the contribution of distinct underlying neurocognitive processes 4. Evidence for this component process account of ongoing thought come from studies showing both common and distinct neuro-

span.label: perceptual decoupling
span.quote: Perceptual decoupling has been suggested to be the result of an insulation mechanism that shields the current train of thought from the potential disruption of processing incoming sensory information4,31,32.

span.label: attentional-state condition (on-task vs off-task; deliberate vs spontaneous)
span.term: attentional-state condition (on-task vs off-task; deliberate vs spontaneous)
span.quote: Parieto-occipital ERP contrasts were evaluated with 2*2*3 repeatedmeasures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with factors condition (COND) x channel location (LOC) x ERP component/ time interval (TIME).

span.label: self-reported category of ongoing thought at the probe
span.term: self-reported category of ongoing thought at the probe
span.quote: Once triggered, thought-probes presented participants with the question "Where was your mind just now?" and prompted them to classify their immediately preceding thoughts by choosing between five possible answers

span.label: ERP component amplitude (P1, N1, P2, N2, P3)
span.term: ERP component amplitude (P1, N1, P2, N2, P3)
span.quote: The width of the temporal interval used to measure average component amplitudes were based on the spatial extent and approximate duration of each component.

span.label: band-limited power in the selected time-frequency windows
span.term: band-limited power in the selected time-frequency windows
span.quote: For each selected window all time-frequency points were averaged and submitted to a repeated-measure ANOVA (COND*TFW).

span.label: inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC)
span.quote: Lastly, two-tailed t-tests were found to be significant for ITPC values for all averaged channels [t(17)=2.8 p=.012] with increased coherence for dTUT (M: .52; SD: .1) relative to sTUT (M: .45; SD: .1)

span.label: inter-stimulus interval held fixed at 2315 msec across all trials and conditions
span.term: inter-stimulus interval held fixed at 2315 msec across all trials and conditions
span.quote: During the fixed SART, digits from 1 to 9 were displayed in sequence and individually for 250 msec on the center of the monitor with a fixed inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 2315 msec.

span.label: -200 to 0 msec prestimulus baseline applied to every ERP analysis
span.term: -200 to 0 msec prestimulus baseline applied to every ERP analysis
span.quote: A -200 to 0 msec prestimulus baseline was used for all ERP components analysis and visualisation.

span.label: 26 — participants recorded with EEG during the fixed SART
span.quote: Twenty-six participants (12 females, age M: 25 SD: 4.3) with no history of neurological or psychiatric disease volunteered or received partial course credits to participate in the study.

span.label: 71.4% — share of the average 65.3 thought probes per participant that were self-caught rather than probe-caught
span.quote: The task ran for an average of 38.7 min (SD: 4.8) with an average of 65.3 thought probes (SD: 31.2) of which 71.4% were of the SC variant (for an overview see Figure 1).

span.label: 11% — proportion of SART trials that were no-go targets (the digit 6)
span.quote: The "no-go" target to which the participants were instructed to withhold response was the number 6 (11% of the trials) leaving the numbers 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 as "go" stimulus

span.label: 2315 msec — fixed inter-stimulus interval between SART digits
span.quote: During the fixed SART, digits from 1 to 9 were displayed in sequence and individually for 250 msec on the center of the monitor with a fixed inter-stimulus interval (ISI) of 2315 msec.

span.label: 9.3 sec — length of the four-trial pre-probe window taken to reflect the reported attentional state
span.quote: This window, spanning a period of approximately 9.3 sec was chosen a priori for the following reasons:

span.label: 512 Hz — sampling rate of the 64-channel EEG recording
span.quote: 64-channel EEG data was acquired at 512 Hz using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system (biosemi.com) placed according to the international 10-20 system.

span.label: 19 and 18 — subjects retained for the ERP analysis of the on-task/off-task pair and of the deliberate/spontaneous pair
span.quote: All trials that weren't rejected due to artifacts were included in the average for the ERP analysis resulting in a total of 19 and 18 subjects for the condition pairs PC_OT/MW and SC_dTUT/sTUT, respectively.

span.label: t(17)=2.25 p=.038 — test of the alpha-power difference between deliberate and spontaneous off-task pre-trials
span.quote: Follow-up t-tests determined alpha activity (Figure 5, C and supplemental Figure 2, right panel) to be significantly higher during dTUT pre-trials (M:1.54 dB SD: 1.44) when compared to sTUT (M:.58 dB SD: 1.2) [t(17)=2.25 p=.038].

span.label: .52 vs .45 — mean inter-trial phase coherence before deliberate versus spontaneous off-task reports across all averaged channels
span.quote: Lastly, two-tailed t-tests were found to be significant for ITPC values for all averaged channels [t(17)=2.8 p=.012] with increased coherence for dTUT (M: .52; SD: .1) relative to sTUT (M: .45; SD: .1)
